body:
@kreuzzelg thanks — three of your points land squarely, and there is fresh data from last night that belongs in this thread.

**The `S == 1` gate on the dense GPU path was conservatism, not a kernel limit — and I removed it.** `quant_matmul` already launches grid `(O, S)`, `y[s*O+o]` is the same row-major layout the CPU produces, and `coli_cuda_matmul` has always taken `S`. On a rig where prefill is 19.7 s of CPU BF16 GEMM, the pinned BF16 reference costs real wall time, so: a `qt_dense_matmul_batch` wrapper + an opt-in dispatcher branch (`Q38_TRUNK_PREFILL=1`, default keeps your semantics). Measured at 3006 tokens: **TTFT 271.9 → 223.3 s (-17.9%)**, `resident-mm` 105 → 57 s, and **greedy output bit-identical** to the CPU BF16 reference at that context; the `Q38_TRUNK_SELFTEST` batch path is 330/331 matrices at ~1e-7 rel.err. The remaining dense time is placement-bounded (`p_marginal ~0.15` says the small matrices should stay on CPU). Happy to shape this however you want it upstream — including keeping it opt-in.

**The quality point is correct and I accept it.** Greedy-vs-greedy across two tiers that share the same int4 experts measures the trunk, not the container — it cannot see the int4 gs64 cost at all. The arms you asked for are fair and I owe them: greedy against `Q38_TRUNK_GPU=0` on the FP8 checkpoint, and a perplexity run on a fixed text against the same reference. **I'll get those measurements to you as soon as I have the chance** — posting the token file here would let me run your exact 16×512 protocol and keep the numbers comparable across rigs.

**Honest correction to my own battery, before you build on it:** last night's rig turned out to be measuring under memory pressure — zram/swap churn and file-page refaults (PLE preads and non-pinned warm experts) were contaminating A/B deltas. Same binary, same prompt, only the swap state changed: hybrid wall 3.99 → 4.61 tok/s, and the no-trunk arm moved the *other* way without the valve (3.64 → 2.73). So treat the +11%/+40% decode numbers as pending a rebaseline with the memory regime declared and reclaim counters logged per run — I'd rather flag it myself than have it found later. (Your chance-level hot-set overlap from #1424 fits what I'm seeing: the engine re-reads ~1 GB/s of NVMe mid-run on warm expert refaults; the arena's pinned set is precisely why it survives that.)

**On upstream: agreed on both halves.** fmt=9 (bf16 dense) as its own first PR is the cheapest piece — I'll open it. And framing the arena as `qt_note_planned` entries that never evict is better than a parallel tier: it inherits the fake-backend tests and the cudaMalloc-granularity fix falls out of the pool shape for free. and the second data point from your 3070/Quadro pair is genuinely welcome — no need to wait for a PR to spend that offer: the fork is public and [`DebugSultan/colibri` @ `qwen38cuda`](https://github.com/DebugSultan/colibri/tree/qwen38cuda) already carries both pieces — the resident int8 trunk (`Q38_TIER_TRUNK`) and the batched-prefill gate removal (`Q38_TRUNK_PREFILL=1`, with the `Q38_TRUNK_SELFTEST` batch line). The prefill path needs only the trunk placement, not our int4 containers, and on your cards the arena just settles at a lower residency. If a -17.9% TTFT at ~3k tokens replicates on Ampere+Quadro, that is worth knowing before shaping the upstream version.

---

**EDIT 2026-09-19 — the rebaseline I promised above is done, and it corrects two things I said. Same comment edited rather than a new one, so the thread stays readable.**

**1. Fixed memory regime, and this time the regime is part of the measurement.** Prod stopped (GPUs at 2 MiB), `swapoff -a`, preflight verifying `SwapTotal=0 kB`, and per-arm evidence: `pswpin`/`pswpout` delta **0 pages** on all four arms, `read_bytes` 2.4–3.8 MB per run (i.e. no disk I/O during the measurement — 34.70 GB of experts wired with mlock, 0 lock failures), storage probe 5.73 → 5.68 GB/s across the battery, and `parallel-batches` = 1258/1258/2056/1258, all **> 0**, so no arm sat in the `cap < topk` cliff.

**2. The decode numbers I asked you to treat as pending did not survive.** 64 tokens, `CACHE=8192 BITS=8 OMP=20`, 2k prompt, same read-only heat file for every arm: `ours` **0.2193 tok/s** — `hybrid` (`Q38_TIER_TRUNK=2`) **+0.69%** — `hybrid_pf` (`+Q38_TRUNK_PREFILL=1`) **+0.17%** — `trunk` (`Q38_TIER_TRUNK=1`) **−12.39%**. The first two are noise, and the counters say so unambiguously: across `ours`, `hybrid` and `hybrid_pf`, `weight-ranges`, `coalesced-gate-up`, `prefetched`, `parallel-batches`, cache hit rate (92.1%) and the GPU/CPU split (70.1% on GPU) are **identical digit for digit**. So: **the +40%/+11% hybrid gains were an artifact of the contaminated regime — please do not carry them forward.**

**3. The part that concerns your tier directly, and it is my mistake to report.** In that battery your VRAM expert tier showed `VRAM hit rate 0.0% | LFRU swaps 0` in every trunk arm — 553 tensors and ~4.0 GB resident in `trunk`, 16590+16707 tensors and 14.24+14.34 GB in `hybrid_pf`, and **zero hits** in all of them. It was not a policy that never promotes. It was unreachable by construction on my side: my battery sets `Q38_INT4_SNAP`, `q38_load_expert` opens with `if (q38_try_load_int4_expert(...)) return;`, so every expert lands in `i4_slab` and `fp8_slab` stays NULL — and my note hook requires a *native FP8* slot (`ex->fp8_slab && ex->gate.data == ex->fp8_slab`), so `qt_note()` was never called once. `q_skips 0` rules out queue congestion. Positive control, same arm with only `Q38_INT4_SNAP` removed: **`resident 115/24576`, `uploads 115`, hit rate 4.9%** — the tier wakes up exactly as designed.

**Consequence, stated plainly: that −12.39% measures your *dense* int8 trunk (`553 of 553 offered matrices resident as int8`, genuinely active in every arm) with your *expert tier* switched off. On experts, the two designs were never compared. Please do not read it as a verdict on your expert tier — it isn't one, and I would rather correct that here than have it quoted somewhere as if it were.**

For what it is worth, the dense int8 trunk is the best dense path measured on this rig (42.4+33.2 vs 100.6+69.9 ms/fwd), and that result is unaffected by any of the above.

**4. Method note, since it cost me an arm.** I first hypothesised the starving guard came from the mapping branch in `q38_load_native_fp8_ranges` and predicted `COLI_MAP_EXPERTS=0` would wake the tier. Control run: **no change, `miss(CPU) 3360` identical bit for bit**. The chain was coherent and simply not the one being taken. A coherent code path is not a measurement, and the control has to be run on the flag you believe is causal.

The fmt=9 (bf16) PR is now open: #1620, against `dev` @ `5a0b725`, with the test green. It also carries a small NULL-memcpy fix the test caught in `coli_cuda_tensor_update()`.
